statement: Management estimates it is giving up more than $50M of bookings (about 5 points of YoY bookings growth) by reducing friction (ads, subscription upsells) for free users
source_or_basis: Q4/FY2025 shareholder letter dated 2026-02-26 (8-K/A), section 'Reinvest in our free user value proposition': https://investors.duolingo.com/node/11661/html
evidence_status: Verified against primary source; management estimate, not independently verifiable
notes: Always label as 'management's estimate'

statement: Management expects 2026 bookings growth of about 11%, compared with nearly 20% it believes it could achieve operating as in past years
source_or_basis: Q4/FY2025 shareholder letter, CEO section on the 2026 plan (same URL as R01)
evidence_status: Verified against primary source; management counterfactual
notes: Anchors for the 2026 bookings growth of Path B (growth first) and Path A (monetization first)

statement: Management says the old approach would likely mean fewer DAUs and more money per user, and could reach higher bookings in 2028, but a smaller, less valuable business long term
source_or_basis: Q4/FY2025 shareholder letter, CEO section (same URL as R01)
evidence_status: Verified against primary source; management view
notes: Important: on bookings alone Path B may not overtake Path A by 2028. The model must show this honestly

statement: Medium-term goal of reaching 100 million DAUs in 2028
source_or_basis: Q4/FY2025 shareholder letter (same URL as R01)
notes: Letter does not say which measure or quarter. See A02

statement: Management expects about 20% DAU growth in 2026; in August 2026 it said growth should stay above 20% for the rest of the year
evidence_status: Verified against primary source; forward-looking statement
notes: Forecast, not a result

statement: Q2 2026: DAU 58.7M (+23% YoY), total bookings $289.1M (+8%), paid subscribers 12.7M (+17%), adjusted EBITDA margin 25.9% vs 31.2%
evidence_status: Verified against primary source; also in the KPI CSV

statement: FY2026 guidance (Aug 2026): bookings $1,285M (+10.9%), revenue $1,207M, adjusted EBITDA margin about 26.5%
evidence_status: Verified against primary source; guidance = management forecast

statement: Management attributes the Q2 2026 DAU acceleration to product changes, marketing impact and a one-time Streak Revival event (15.4M learners revived streaks, nearly 8M of them had no active streak)
notes: Confounder: Q2 2026 DAU growth is not a clean trend

statement: Q2 2026 bookings growth slowed partly because of a tough prior-year comparison (Energy rollout, price increase and strong advertising in Q2 2025)
notes: Confounder for bookings per DAU in Q2 2026

statement: Current User Retention Rate (share of current-user DAUs who return the next day) is 84%, an all-time high, up about 1 point YoY
evidence_status: Verified against primary source; company-reported, not independently validated
notes: Correlational context only

statement: CEO stated that over 20% of DAUs had streaks longer than a year
evidence_status: Verified against primary source; company-reported; dated 2024
notes: Correlational context only

statement: Management believes the extra friction (more ads, subscription upsells) is part of the reason DAU growth slowed
evidence_status: Verified against primary source; management's stated belief
notes: This is the stated rationale. The data alone do not demonstrate causation

statement: DAU/MAU = DAU divided by MAU, both quarterly averages
notes: From 2026 Duolingo calls MAU a supplementary metric

statement: Bookings per DAU (quarterly) = total bookings divided by quarterly average DAU. Includes advertising, English Test and in-app purchases; it is not revenue per user; Q4 is seasonally high
notes: Falling every year since 2023, so most of the decline PREDATES the Feb 2026 strategy shift. Compare the same quarter across years only

statement: Paid subscribers per DAU = period-end paid subscribers divided by quarterly average DAU (mixed basis)
notes: Not the same as paid conversion of MAU, which Duolingo reports on a trailing basis

statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin = adjusted EBITDA divided by revenue
evidence_status: Matches the margins printed in the letters

statement: DAU growth needed per year to go from 52.7M (Q4 2025) to 100M by Q4 2028
notes: Above today's 20-23%, so the goal requires acceleration

statement: Annual bookings per average DAU = fiscal-year total bookings divided by the average of the four quarterly DAUs. Basis for the break-even model
notes: Define it the same way for both paths

statement: Both paths are compared on cumulative total bookings over the same period
source_or_basis: Avoids comparing users in one path with revenue in the other
notes: Keep the unit and time basis identical for both paths

statement: The 100M DAU goal means quarterly average DAU in Q4 2028
notes: State it in the README

statement: Path B (growth first): 2026 bookings growth about 11% and DAU growth about 20-24% (management figures). Later years are adjustable
notes: Years after 2026 are my assumptions

statement: Path A (monetization first): 2026 bookings growth about 20% (R02); DAU growth lower than Path B
source_or_basis: Management gives no DAU figure for this path
notes: Show a range and a sensitivity view

statement: Bookings per DAU after 2026 under each path (recovery or continued decline)
notes: Main driver of the break-even point

statement: Scorecard thresholds: green = on or ahead of the path needed for break-even; amber = within the historical quarter-to-quarter variation; red = beyond it
source_or_basis: Historical variation of YoY growth in the KPI CSV
evidence_status: Method defined; values to be derived
notes: No arbitrary percentages

statement: Streak evidence (R08, R10, R11) is correlational context only; no causal claim about the streak
source_or_basis: Public data cannot isolate the streak
